cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing this letter to everyone in Rome who is loved by God (Romans 1:1, 7). He just said a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart (Romans 2:29). That raises a question: what's the advantage of being a Jew, or the value of circumcision?

cards.question: Paul says being a Jew still has an advantage, much in every way.

cards.text: Then Paul names the first advantage on his list.

cards.question: What's the first advantage of being a Jew that Paul names?

answers.text: They were trusted with God's very words
They were spared from God's judgment
They were made rulers over the nations

cards.text: Then Paul asks a hard one. What if some of them did not have faith?

cards.question: If some of the people trusted with God's words don't have faith, does that cancel out God's faithfulness?

cards.text: Paul says, "Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar." Every man, friend, and that includes the stamper who told the dough "back in one minute" and came back after a NAP.

cards.question: Paul backs it up by quoting Psalm 51:4, a line about God speaking and judging. How does God come out?

cards.text: Now Paul tries out a tricky idea, speaking in human terms, as he puts it. If our unrighteousness highlights God's righteousness, is God unjust to bring His wrath on us?

cards.question: Paul agrees that God would be unjust to bring His wrath on people whose unrighteousness highlights His righteousness.
Paul's reason: if God were unjust, how could He ___ the world?

cards.text: Paul tries the idea one more way, this time with "my falsehood." Same argument, new apron.

cards.question: Paul asks: if his lie made God's ___ shine even brighter, why would he still be condemned as a sinner?

cards.text: Follow that thinking all the way and you land on a line that some people slanderously claim Paul and others say.

cards.question: What's the line some people slanderously claim Paul and others say?

answers.text: Let us do evil that good may result
Let us obey so that we may be blessed
Let us rest so that God may work

cards.text: That's like burning a batch ON PURPOSE so the next one looks amazing. Paul's last word on it: "Their condemnation is deserved!"
Paul asks, "What then? Are we any better?" He answers not at all, and says he's already made the charge about who's under sin.

cards.question: Paul says he's already made the charge. Who is under sin?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes Psalm 14: "There is no one righteous, not even one." I had my mustache halfway up to say, "Well, what about ME?"

cards.question: In Paul's quote from Psalm 14, there is no one who seeks God.
Paul's quote keeps going about everyone. What have all of them done?

cards.text: No one understands, all have together become worthless, and "there is no one who does good, not even one." That's the second "not even one," friend, so my mustache is coming DOWN.
Next Paul quotes Psalm 5:9 and Psalm 140:3: their throats are open graves, their tongues practice deceit, and the venom of vipers is on their lips. Friend, that viper venom is NOT lip balm.

cards.question: Then Paul quotes Psalm 10:7 about people's mouths. What are their mouths full of?

cards.text: Paul quotes Isaiah 59:7-8, and the picture goes down to the feet: "Their feet are swift to shed blood; ruin and misery lie in their wake…" I think this one hurts.

cards.question: In Paul's quote from Isaiah, these people have known the way of peace.

cards.text: Last stop on this tour of the body: the eyes, in Paul's quote from Psalm 36:1. And friend, it's about what's NOT in front of them.

cards.question: In Paul's last quote, what is missing before people's eyes?

cards.text: Now Paul turns from the quotes to something "we know": whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law. Like a recipe card, it's talking to whoever's standing at the oven.

cards.question: Paul says the law speaks to those under it so that the whole ___ is held accountable to God.

cards.text: Every mouth silenced, friend. EVERY mouth, even one as loud as Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids and the loudest voice in the Millers' kitchen.

cards.question: Paul says a person can be justified in God's sight by works of the law.
Paul says the law merely brings awareness of ___.
